root_cause.text: The GRO merge function `skb_gro_receive()` copies frags between skbs without checking whether either skb uses zero-copy (managed frag refs), and because zero-copy skbs do not hold page references, merging frags without adjusting the page refcount causes a use-after-free when pages are freed prematurely.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message states "skb_gro_receive() can currently copy frags between the source and GRO skb, without checking the zerocopy status, and in particular the SKBFL_MANAGED_FRAG_REFS flag. When SKBFL_MANAGED_FRAG_REFS is set, the skb doesn't hold a reference on the pages in shinfo->frags. Appending those frags to another skb's frags without fixing up the page refcount can lead to UAF." The patch enforces `if (skb_zcopy(p) || skb_zcopy(skb)) return -ETOOMANYREFS;` to prevent merging.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to return error in skb_gro_receive if either skb uses zero-copy, preventing unsafe merging.
intent_record.what: Added a check that returns -ETOOMANYREFS if either the existing skb (p) or the new skb (skb) has zero-copy (skb_zcopy) data.
intent_record.how: This prevents the GRO merge from proceeding when either packet uses zero-copy buffers, avoiding potential memory management issues.

candidates.rationale: This condition is the only existing guard against mismatched page recycling, but it does not check for zero-copy skbs (which use managed frag refs and lack page references). When this condition is false, the merge proceeds without ensuring that the skbs are safe to merge, leading to use-after-free.
